ok.de: Nach Never before steht das Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt: Never before have we seen.
ok.en: After Never before, the auxiliary comes before the subject: Never before have we seen.

wrong.de: Nach Never before kommt have vor we: have we seen.
wrong.en: After Never before, have comes before we: have we seen.

items.after: can the system open to all users.

ok.de: Should you need … ist eine förmliche Bedingung ohne if und ohne will.
ok.en: Should you need … is a formal condition without if and without will.

wrong.en: After Should you the base form follows, no will.

items.lead: If you need further details, simply reply to this email.
items.after: further details, simply reply to this email.

ok.de: Were it not for + Nomen heißt „wenn nicht … gewesen wäre“.

items.after: the support of our partners, we could not have finished on time.

ok.de: Hardly had we opened … when … Nach Hardly steht had vor dem Subjekt.
ok.en: Hardly had we opened … when … After Hardly, had stands before the subject.

wrong.en: After Hardly, had comes before we: had we.

items.after: opened the report when the phone rang.

ok.de: Das betonte does steht vor der Grundform know.
ok.en: The stressed does stands before the base form know.

wrong.en: After does the base form know follows.

ok.en: The stressed did stands before the base form send.

wrong.en: After did the base form send follows.

ok.de: Such was the demand that … Das Verb steht vor dem Subjekt.
ok.en: Such was the demand that … The verb stands before the subject.

ok.en: I hope not. Not follows the verb directly and replaces the thought.
